kind: LIVE ESP dataplane test (EXP-10 addendum) - 5 ICMP echo/reply pairs through a real strongSwan<->OpenBSD iked tunnel
topology: same isolated Parallels Host-Only network as obsd-vendor.pcap (10.37.129.0/24); T0 vantage = macOS host bridge101
why_this_capture_exists: obsd-vendor.pcap (the original EXP-10 capture) had 0 ESP packets because no traffic was pushed through the tunnel. This follow-up explicitly sends ICMP through the established SA to test whether macOS's kernel actually enforces the IPsec policy despite charon logging '[KNL] can't install route ... conflicts with IKE traffic', and to validate TunnelScope's ESP-level extractors (cipher sieve, leakage) against real OpenBSD-side dataplane traffic for the first time.

flows: flow esp in from 10.37.129.2 to 10.37.129.50 peer 10.37.129.2 srcid IPV4/10.37.129.50 dstid IPV4/10.37.129.2 type require
flow esp out from 10.37.129.50 to 10.37.129.2 peer 10.37.129.2 srcid IPV4/10.37.129.50 dstid IPV4/10.37.129.2 type require
sad: esp tunnel from 10.37.129.2 to 10.37.129.50 spi 0xae499361 enc aes-256-gcm
esp tunnel from 10.37.129.50 to 10.37.129.2 spi 0xc924358f enc aes-256-gcm

finding_1_route_warning_is_nonfatal.claim: charon's '[KNL] can't install route ... conflicts with IKE traffic' warning does NOT mean the SA is unenforced
finding_1_route_warning_is_nonfatal.evidence: all 10 captured packets (5 ping request + 5 reply) are genuine ESP (ip.proto=50) with the exact SPIs (0xae499361 out, 0xc924358f in) that both sides' T2 state shows for this SA - real dataplane traffic flowed correctly despite the warning

finding_2_tfc_heuristic_false_positive.claim: TunnelScope's TFC-padding-active heuristic (tunnelscope/leakage/leakage.py: 'padding_active = distinct <= 1 and len(lens) >= 5') produces a FALSE POSITIVE on this capture
finding_2_tfc_heuristic_false_positive.why_wrong: OpenBSD iked was not configured with any TFC/dummy-padding option in this test. The 10 ESP frames are uniform in size because all 5 ICMP echo/reply pairs sent were themselves identical-size probes (default ping payload) - naturally uniform traffic, not active padding. The heuristic (>=5 packets, <=1 distinct length) cannot distinguish 'traffic happens to be uniform' from 'padding is forcing uniformity', because EXP-05's original synthetic dataset always paired non-uniform 'unpadded' traffic against uniform 'padded' traffic and never tested naturally-uniform unpadded traffic as its own case.
finding_2_tfc_heuristic_false_positive.status: genuine, newly-found limitation - not fixed this session, recorded honestly as a follow-up

tunnelscope_esp_extraction.esp_cipher_family: INFERRED ['AES-CBC+HMAC-SHA256-128','AES-CTR+HMAC-SHA256-128','AES-GCM-16','AES-CCM-16','ChaCha20-Poly1305'] - correctly did not exclude the true cipher (AES-GCM-16 family), consistent with EXP-01's one-directional sieve design; uniform small ICMP frames give the sieve no additional narrowing signal here

note: Ground truth is T2 (OpenBSD ipsecctl -sa, causal), never TunnelScope's own inference, per DEC-009.
